notes: This contract pins the embedded transport fault path to the Requirements Lab's explicit Connection Lost requirements. The private loopback endpoint drives the same failure handler a future remote transport will use; Catch2 verifies the official callback, forced Not Connected lifecycle, membership removal, reconnect boundary, and the separate selected-file service-report record that is appended before the callback while the lost member still owns its writer. It also covers configured DELETE_OBJECTS, UNCONDITIONALLY_DIVEST_ATTRIBUTES, DELETE_OBJECTS_THEN_DIVEST, CANCEL_PENDING_OWNERSHIP_ACQUISITIONS, and CANCEL_THEN_DELETE_THEN_DIVEST Automatic Resign Directive dispositions through the official support-service setter, plus the bounded NO_ACTION forced-resign policy: retain the known object, divest the departed member's owned attributes, offer those attributes to an eligible survivor, and do not emit an automatic Remove Object Instance callback. Focused equal-to and strict-less-than cutoff regressions capture a lost time regulator's granted position before forced resignation and release already queued ordinary and directed timestamped interactions, timestamped attribute-update passels, and timestamped object removals at or before that position to a remaining constrained subscriber. The ordinary-interaction equality case covers both a TAR pending at loss and one submitted later; the directed cases prove forced source resignation does not suppress an accepted payload while the target and current recipient selector remain valid, including a DELETE_OBJECTS target whose recipient opens its boundary only after the loss; the attribute-update cases preserve a reliable reflection's metadata through the loss, drain the same accepted passel to two survivors that request time 6 at different moments, and keep a cutoff reflection distinct from a DELETE_OBJECTS-generated receive-order removal whether the TAR was already pending or submitted after the loss. If a changed declaration legitimately suppresses that queued reflection at the callback boundary, its recipient ledger is terminally suppressed rather than left pending, so the reserved automatic removal releases through the next receive-order gate; the two-survivor cleanup case proves those removal reservations release independently. With asynchronous delivery enabled, evoked and immediate attribute counterparts prove reflection precedes its matching grant and the now-eligible receive-order automatic removal follows in that same TAR. The deletion cases preserve marked time-5/time-6 removals through unconditional-divest cleanup, drain a common removal to two survivors that request time 6 at different moments, and prevent DELETE_OBJECTS cleanup from replacing a marked time-6 removal with a receive-order callback. A complementary asynchronous-delivery case proves that the same time-6 cutoff is carried in the subscribed survivor's HLAreportFederateLost parameter while its timestamp-6 interaction reaches the matching grant. These cases deliberately make no assertion about a message later than that position, because the source permits either outcome. The closest Lab candidate for the required auto-resign step ends before its continuation names the directive; RL-060 records that extraction limitation, while RL-070 records the split cross-cutting page-50 export. It is source/test traceability only, not protected-review evidence, a production transport claim, or conformance evidence.
